title: One machine step
statement: For a program $P$ and a configuration with program counter $p$ and memory $m$, one step returns either a new configuration or a Boolean terminal result. If the instruction at $p$ is missing, it is treated as rejection. An instruction that writes a value to address $i$ stores that $W$-bit value at $i$ and advances the counter to $p+1$; the arithmetic instructions write the corresponding word addition, subtraction, or multiplication, and load and store use the integer value represented by a word as an address. A negative-value branch jumps to its specified position exactly when the tested word represents a negative integer, and otherwise advances to $p+1$; accept and reject return true and false, respectively.
